review.summary: OSWorld makes a substantial benchmark contribution by providing a controllable real-computer environment and diverse tasks with per-task executable evaluation, enabling assessment beyond browser-only or static-demonstration settings. Careful construction and human/baseline measurements make it useful, while empirical conclusions remain bounded by its Ubuntu-centered task suite and disclosed evaluation uncertainty.

observations.claim: The benchmark’s task coverage and execution-based setup support evaluation of multi-application workflows, with substantial annotation and quality-check effort.
observations.quote: each example is further scrutinized and iterated upon by different individuals three times from the perspective of alignment with the instruction and correctness under different solutions

observations.claim: Human evaluation establishes a meaningful capability gap on the benchmark.
observations.quote: the human performance on our tasks was approximately 72.36%

observations.claim: The paper notes residual evaluator error risk despite extensive checks, relevant to interpreting execution-based scores.
observations.quote: Further investment of time and a more red teaming could further reduce false positives and negatives, which we will leave to future work.

observations.claim: The primary task suite is Ubuntu-centered; Windows is supplementary in the inspected material.
observations.quote: We introduce the OSW ORLD benchmark, which encompasses 369 real computing tasks defined and executed on Ubuntu.

unresolved_questions: How robust are success rates to alternative valid completion paths and evaluator edge cases across the full task suite?
I inspected pages 1 and 6–10, but not the remaining methods, full ablations, or later discussion; what additional experimental details or limitations do those sections report?
